subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 Consolidation: Grammar file and Practice Guide
outcomes: Use the past simple and past continuous correctly.
Use the -ing form as a subject and after prepositions.
Use reading and speaking exam strategies from the Practice Guide.

tf.s: We use the past continuous for a longer action that was in progress in the past.
'I was believing everything he said' is correct.
tf.why: Believe is a stative verb, so we say 'I believed'.

tf.s: We can use the -ing form as the subject of a sentence: 'Swimming is fun.'
tf.why: The -ing form can act like a noun.

tf.s: The past simple question of 'you saw' is 'Did you saw?'
tf.why: After did we use the base verb: 'Did you see?'

tf.s: A past simple action can interrupt a past continuous action.
tf.why: I was tidying my room when my cousin arrived.

tf.s: The negative of 'I was considering' is 'I wasn't considering'.
After a preposition we use the base form: 'interested in learn'.
tf.why: After a preposition we use -ing: interested in learning.

tf.s: A distractor is a wrong option that may contain words from the text.
tf.why: Distractors can look right but don't match the meaning.

tf.s: The last question in a long-text reading task usually tests a small detail.
tf.why: It usually tests the main idea or the writer's overall opinion.

tf.s: There are five short texts in Reading Part 1.
tf.why: Reading Part 1 has five short texts.

boxes.q: Complete: I ___ the message because I ___.
boxes.why: Short finished action + longer action in progress.

boxes.q: Complete: ___ to music helps me relax.

boxes.why: Stative verbs don't use the continuous.

boxes.q: Which is a past simple question?
What should you look for between a text and the options?
boxes.why: Words with the same meaning help you match.
Distractors are there to test careful reading.

boxes.q: Complete: I was tidying my room when my cousin ___.
boxes.why: The short action interrupts: past simple.
Stative verbs describe states, like believe or know.

boxes.q: Where can you check your answers to Practice Guide tasks?
boxes.why: The explanations show why answers are right or wrong.

mcq.q: Which form do we use for a longer action in progress at a time in the past?
Which is the correct past continuous question?
Which sentence uses the -ing form as a subject?
mcq.why: The -ing word is the subject here.

mcq.q: What does the last question in Reading Part 3 usually test?
o: the main idea or the writer's opinion
mcq.why: It tests your understanding of the whole text.

mcq.q: Complete: I ___ (do) my homework when the phone ___ (ring).
mcq.why: Long action in progress, then a short interruption.

o: I'm thinking about talking to her.
I'm thinking about talk to her.
I'm thinking about talked to her.
I'm thinking about to talk to her.

mcq.q: Choose the correct sentence with a stative verb.
Why can an option be wrong even if it has words from the text?
o: Its meaning doesn't match all the information in the text
It is always the first option
mcq.why: Read for meaning, not only for the same words.

mcq.q: Why is 'I was hearing a noise' usually wrong?
o: Hear is normally stative, so we say 'I heard a noise'
mcq.why: Stative verbs usually don't take the continuous.

mcq.q: Which strategy helps you most in multiple-choice reading?
o: Underline key words and find the matching part of the text
mcq.why: Key words lead you to the evidence.
